Memory chip stocks are up in premarket trading Monday, with Micron (NASDAQ:MU) climbing 1.3%, Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) gaining 1.2%, and SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) rising 2.5%. The gains follow encouraging comments from Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya, who believes the industry’s supply shortages could persist longer than investors previously anticipated.

Following meetings with Micron executives in New York and Boston, Arya came away more confident about the industry’s outlook. One particularly encouraging takeaway was the company’s expectation that memory supplies could become even tighter in 2027 and 2028 than during 2026.
